title: Cycle-25 A.4 witness-mechanism viability discriminator (cycle 24 follow-up) + cycle-29 option (c) self-allocated witness
purpose: Minimal real-Xbox-only diagnostic XBE that fires the cycle-23 A.4 kseg0-scan witness twice (stages MAIN_ENTERED=1 + POST_MARKER0=3) with 500 ms sleep gaps, then HalReturnToFirmware(HalRebootRoutine)s. Cycle 29 ADDED an option (c) self-witness AFTER the existing cycle-23 fires (Codex round-1 high finding #1 adopted — ordering keeps the cycle-23 path bit-identical to cycle 25 up to and including the second cycle-23 fire): after the unchanged cycle-23 fires + 500 ms inter-fire sleep, main() also calls xbed_self_witness_fire(MAIN_ENTERED) + xbed_self_witness_fire(POST_MARKER0), which allocates the XBE's OWN persistent contiguous page via MmAllocateContiguousMemoryEx + MmPersistContiguousMemory and stamps a unique 'WTNS' magic + reserved0=(0xA4<<24)|stage + reserved1=counter at known offsets in that page. The relaunched cycle-29 oracle-agent (commit on `apple-silicon-performance`) exposes a new read-only witness.scan-self verb that enumerates 'WTNS' pages in kseg0 [0x80010000, 0x84000000]. NO pbkit, NO NV2A, NO XVideoSetMode, NO file I/O, NO xbed_init. The intermediate marker helper (image-blit's `image_blit_marker(0, ...)` fopen) is REPLACED with a passive `Sleep(500)` — a successful cycle-26 outcome therefore proves the witness mechanism is real-Xbox-safe in this minimal context but does NOT independently exclude the marker helper as a contributor to image-blit's hang. Built via lib/lib.mk so it links xbed_a4_witness.c exactly the way image-blit does — keeps the cycle-25-vs-cycle-21-image-blit binary delta isolated to (a) the absence of pbkit/NV2A/draw-loop, (b) the absence of the marker helper, and (c) main()'s body shrinking. Cycle 26 (Hermes-scheduled) ran the XBE on real Xbox and observed outcome D (no XCTR stamp landed); cycle 28 (cycle-27 preserve-branch oracle-agent) reproduced D-cycle-27 and INVALIDATED the 'stamp landed and got wiped' hypothesis. Cycle 30 (Hermes's call) will deploy the cycle-29 build as a (γ)-only discriminator: a witness.scan-self hit proves main() ran but does NOT discriminate (α) 'scan can't find XCTR' from (β) 'scan finds XCTR but write faults'. Both (α) and (β) remain live even on cycle-30 E1 success; α-vs-β discrimination requires cycle 31+ option (b). The cycle-23 ordering decision (XCTR fires first, self-witness fires second) keeps the cycle-23 XCTR readback bit-comparable to cycle 28. See README.md for the full discriminator semantics table + cycle-29 addendum.

witness_readback.notes: Cycle 26: after chainload reboots Xbox to dashboard FTP and the oracle agent is re-launched, run `oracle-client.py raw witness.scan`. With cycle-27 option (a) active (oracle-agent commit on `apple-silicon-performance`), `s_allocate_fresh` preserves an A.4-stamped header across agent re-launch when the kernel pool returns the same persistent phys (the cycle-26-observed behavior on this Xbox), so a successful witness fire can surface EITHER (i) as an orphan with reserved[0] == 0xA4xxxxxx (legacy orphan shape) OR (ii) as the LIVE buffer itself carrying reserved[0] == 0xA4xxxxxx (cycle-27 preserve-branch shape). Expected payloads: 0xA4000003 (both fires landed; witness mechanism real-Xbox-safe IN THIS MINIMAL XBE; marker helper exclusion requires a follow-on cycle) | 0xA4000001 (first fire only; second fire hung box but soft-reset eventually triggered) | (no readback because Xbox is hung indefinitely) | live=1 reserved0=0 (witness writes never landed; mechanism real-Xbox-incompatible OR fires returned phys=0). Cycle 29 adds the cycle-29 option (c) readback via the new `witness.scan-self` verb (sister verb to `witness.scan`): enumerates kseg0 pages with the diag-XBE's OWN 'WTNS' magic + version 1 + plausibility-filter on reserved[0,1]. After a cycle-30 chainload + relaunched cycle-27/29 agent, both verbs should be queried — witness.scan reports the cycle-23 XCTR-scan outcome (same shapes as cycle 28) AND witness.scan-self reports the cycle-29 self-allocated-page outcome. The two readbacks together discriminate (α) vs (γ); see expected_results.real-xbox/physical/cycle-30 for the full shape table.

real-xbox/physical/cycle-26.notes: Cycle 26 expected outcome A (witness mechanism real-Xbox-safe IN THIS MINIMAL XBE): Xbox reboots in ~5..15 s; agent witness.scan after re-launch shows either (i) LEGACY ORPHAN SHAPE: a NEW orphan (separate phys from the live buffer) with reserved[0] == 0xA4000003 and reserved[1] == 2, OR (ii) CYCLE-27 PRESERVE-BRANCH SHAPE (active once the oracle-agent commit on `apple-silicon-performance` lands): live buffer itself carrying reserved[0] == 0xA4000003 and reserved[1] == 2, on the cycle-26-observed reused phys (e.g. 0x03eb3000) — the agent's tightened `s_allocate_fresh` plausibility gate preserves the witness header instead of memset-wiping it. Cycle-26 outcome D (`a31e061144`) revealed that on this Xbox the kernel pool deterministically returns the same persistent phys across agent re-launches, so the live-buffer shape is the EXPECTED success surface for cycle 27 readbacks. If the cycle-26 run is repeated within a single power session without an intervening power-cycle, additional A.4-tagged buffers may accumulate; Hermes must verify the hard precondition (exactly ONE live buffer with reserved[0] == 0 BEFORE chainload) holds for every attempt. Outcome A discriminator scope: image-blit's hang is in code ABSENT from witness-only (pbkit / NV2A / xbed_init / xbed_render_loop_then_capture AND the image_blit_marker helper). Independently excluding the marker helper requires a follow-on cycle that exercises it between the two fires. Outcome B (witness mechanism real-Xbox-incompatible): Xbox hangs identically to cycle-24 image-blit (no FTP/21 / agent/9001 / ICMP ping response for 5+ minutes). Outcome C (less likely): Xbox reboots + a stamped (orphan or live) buffer with reserved[0] == 0xA4000001 (MAIN_ENTERED stamped; POST_MARKER0 hung the box and a watchdog soft-reset eventually fired).

xemu-metal/canonical/cycle-25-local-smok.notes: Cycle-25 local xemu-Metal validation (this cycle, NOT cycle-26): with XEMU_GUEST_LOG=1 the XBE emits 'witness-only: main() entered (cycle 25)' + 'xbed_a4_witness: enter stage=1' + 'witness-only: fire1 returned phys=...' + 'xbed_a4_witness: enter stage=3' + 'witness-only: fire2 returned phys=...' + 'witness-only: rebooting via HalReturnToFirmware(HalRebootRoutine)' to xemu stderr. Standalone xemu has no oracle agent running so the witness scan reports 'no XCTR buffer found' and fire1/fire2 both return phys=0x00000000 — this is EXPECTED and proves only that the witness mechanism runs to completion in emulation; it does NOT predict real-Xbox behavior (xemu's MmGetPhysicalAddress emulation cannot reproduce real-Xbox MMIO-aliasing failure modes). Cycle-25 local validation is a smoke test only; the real discriminator answer lives in cycle 26.

real-xbox/physical/cycle-30.notes: Cycle 30 (Hermes-scheduled — NOT this session): deploy the cycle-29 oracle-agent + cycle-29 witness-only XBEs on real Xbox. Canonical cycle-26-style sequence (reachability probe -> baseline witness.scan + witness.scan-self preconditions -> reboot to dashboard -> FTP-upload both XBEs -> ensure-agent -> chainload witness-only -> poll FTP/21+agent/9001+ICMP until dashboard FTP returns -> ensure-agent -> query witness.scan AND witness.scan-self). Discriminator scope (Codex round-1 high finding #2 adopted): cycle-29 readback is positioned narrowly as a (γ)-only discriminator. A witness.scan-self hit proves main() ran AND writes to a self-owned persistent page survive the chainload; it does NOT exercise the failing write into the agent's XCTR page, so cause (β) 'scan finds XCTR but write faults silently' REMAINS LIVE even on success. Breaking α-vs-β requires cycle 31+ option (b). Expected outcomes: (E1 — full success) witness.scan D-cycle-27 (`count=1 live=1 reserved0=0 reserved1=0`) AND witness.scan-self `count=1 reserved0=0xA4000003 reserved1=2` => main() ran AND BOTH self-witness fires landed AND self-allocated WTNS page is findable from non-agent process context => (γ) INVALIDATED; (α) AND (β) both REMAIN LIVE; cycle 31 promotes option (b) for α-vs-β discrimination. (E1' — partial: first self-fire only) witness.scan D-cycle-27 AND witness.scan-self `count=1 reserved0=0xA4000001 reserved1=1` => main() reached self-fire-1 but a soft watchdog reset fired between self-fire-1 and self-fire-2 OR self-fire-2's write did not propagate. (γ) INVALIDATED in the self-fire-1 sense; same α-vs-β follow-up as E1. (E1'' — allocated-but-not-stamped: very unlikely) witness.scan D-cycle-27 AND witness.scan-self `count=1 reserved0=0 reserved1=0` => page allocated + magic/version stamped but neither stage write survived; reader tolerates this shape because it matches the canonical fresh-allocation header; cycle 31 instrument the writer. (E2 — γ leading) witness.scan-self `count=0` AND witness.scan unchanged => no stamp landed anywhere => (γ) leading + cycle-22 pre-main-crash hypothesis re-strengthens; cycle 31+ promotes option (d) on-screen breadcrumb. (E3 — both mechanisms work) witness.scan A1 or A2 success shape (cycle-27 preserve-branch shape) AND witness.scan-self `count=1 reserved0=0xA4000003 reserved1=2` => cycle-26/28 readbacks must have been observation-side artifacts; full re-validation required. (E4 — hang) Xbox hangs identically to cycle 24's 928 s indefinite hang => the cycle-29 own-page allocation OR the new cycle-23-then-cycle-29-fires ordering is a new failure mode; redesign required. (E5 — accumulated orphans) witness.scan-self `count>=2` matching pattern => repeated cycle-30 attempts in same physical power session; power-cycle the Xbox between attempts. Note (Codex round-3 low finding adopted): the listed outcomes are representative, NOT exhaustive. The agent reader accepts any tagged WTNS page with reserved0's top byte == 0xA4 AND reserved1 in [1, 4096]; partial-success edge cases like `reserved0=0xA4000003 reserved1=1` (second self-fire stage byte stamped but first fire's counter increment did not propagate) are tolerated by the reader and should be interpreted as γ-invalidating with the counter + stage byte pinpointing how far main() got.
